clue.text: Separate? That sounds tactful

indicators.note: says the word wanted only has the same sound as the word given, not the same spelling

parts.note: tactful means discreet, said the same way as the spelling meaning separate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether splitting up is the polite thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCREET (tactful) and DISCRETE (separate) are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete describes things that are distinct, individually countable units rather than continuous.

clue.text: Empty deal secured by Ray produces pandemonium

indicators.note: something secured by another thing is held within it

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of deal

explanation.surface: A bad bargain struck with a man called Ray causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedlam was the nickname of Bethlem, a London hospital for the insane, hence a scene of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a London asylum, is a common word for a scene of uproar and chaos.

clue.text: Fool turning up at game could need it for entry

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the document rather than a synonym

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: An idiot who turns up at the match may be asked for identification at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: SAP reversed gives PAS, followed by SPORT: PAS-SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers must show this official travel document to be allowed into a foreign country.

clue.text: Collier left off, possibly to start back

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several possible arrangements of the remaining letters
with something off, it has been taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A coal miner quits work, perhaps to begin heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one L from COLLIER to leave COLIER, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: To start back is to flinch or jump away suddenly in fright, exactly what recoiling means.

clue.text: Labourer's time with tanker

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an oiler is a ship that carries oil

explanation.surface: A worker's shift spent aboard an oil ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiler is someone who works hard at physical tasks, much like any manual worker.

clue.text: Stumble at old style exam

parts.note: to stumble is to trip
OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the calendar before 1752

explanation.surface: A student falters in an old-fashioned examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the final honours examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge undergraduates sit the Tripos, their degree examinations taken in several parts.

clue.text: Fixed look by old boy recalled in pavilion

parts.note: a fixed look is a gaze

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old school pupil stares, remembering times in the cricket pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small summerhouse or garden structure, a kind of open pavilion with a roof.

clue.text: Overhead expenses of serviceman in big time

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, as on clothing labels
a non-commissioned officer, a soldier
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A soldier's running costs mount up over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: NCO goes inside OS-T: O-NCO-S-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncost is a running cost of a business not tied to a particular product, i.e. an overhead.

clue.text: Atlantic c-call, having phoned around outside

indicators.note: one part goes outside another, enclosing it
letters moved around are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a call is a ring, and the stammered c- tells you to stammer the first letter of the word too

explanation.surface: A stammered transatlantic call after someone has rung round.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer printed in c-call is the hint: stammer the synonym for call in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Herring-pond is a jocular old name for the North Atlantic, the ocean crossed between Britain and America.

clue.text: A contribution to what chief is calculating about revenue

indicators.note: the letters make a contribution to the phrase, forming just a piece of it

parts.note: found across chief is calculating

explanation.surface: A donation towards whatever the boss is working out about income.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal relates to government taxation and public money, i.e. concerning revenue.

clue.text: Settle directions to get cake with currants initially inside

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a scone is a small cake

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of currants

explanation.surface: Instructions for a fruit cake recipe, telling the baker to let it settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Directions here means compass points, not recipe instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce yourself is to settle comfortably and securely into a place.

clue.text: Move aimlessly when vehicle's cut dead

indicators.note: something cut has a part removed

parts.note: a moped is a small motorbike
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Drifting about after your car's engine has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D away from MOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope about is to wander listlessly or dejectedly without purpose.

clue.text: Not exactly in round numbers

definitions.meaning: second meaning: roughly, as an approximation

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves mean roughly, so the definitions overlap closely.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning approximately, which matches both an imprecise statement and rounded figures.

clue.text: Damage from use of two water sources

wordplay.note: the River Wear and a teardrop from the eye, two sources of water joined by and

explanation.surface: A dam suffering harm from a pair of springs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England; a tear is water from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is the idiom for gradual deterioration caused by ordinary everyday use.

clue.text: Club member doing a good turn?

definitions.text: Club member doing a good turn?

parts.words: Club member doing a good turn?
parts.note: surface reading: a member of some society performing a kind act
setter's reading: turning, rotating, hints at the name of a famous charitable club

explanation.walkthrough: Rotary clubs do charitable work, and rotary also means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Rotary International, the service club devoted to charity and good works.

clue.text: An uplifting craft for many

parts.note: surface reading: a hobby or skill that cheers lots of people
setter's reading: a vessel that lifts its passengers into the sky

explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like a handicraft, and uplifting like inspiring; really it is a vehicle that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aircraft carries many people up into the sky on scheduled flights.

clue.text: Pale-coloured metal in road sign?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a word painted on roads as a warning
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A faded metal plate used for a traffic sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the road sign is the word painted on the tarmac, not a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes an unhealthy yellowish, pale complexion or colour.

clue.text: Servant with endless ailment upset

indicators.note: upset suggests being knocked over into disorder
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A domestic worker distressed by a chronic illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T from AILMENT, then rearrange AILMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic worker doing lowly household tasks, an old word for a servant.

clue.text: The farm building's a main element in Devon

definitions.note: names a place found in Devon rather than giving a synonym

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
a staple is a principal item or basic element

explanation.surface: The barn is a key feature of the rural West Country landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a town situated in north Devon, on the estuary of the River Taw.

clue.text: Mother's essential character?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the natural world personified as Mother ...
second meaning: a thing's basic qualities

explanation.surface: Wondering what Mum is really like at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase Mother Nature personifies the natural world, and a person's nature is their inherent temperament.

clue.text: Take on board complaint arising — a cough?

indicators.note: in a down entry, arising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is a medical complaint
a harsh cough is called a bark

explanation.surface: An illness developing on a ship, with someone hacking away.
explanation.walkthrough: ME reversed gives EM, then BARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or to load passengers or cargo onto it.

clue.text: Angler's equipment is authentic, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: authentic means genuine, said the same way as the fishing device

explanation.surface: Assurance that a fisherman's gear is the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman winds the line on a reel, the spool attached to the rod.

clue.text: Inflator? Hardly!

definitions.note: the whole clue: the opposite of a device that puffs things up

indicators.note: hardly suggests the word has been forced roughly into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: An inflator blows things up; this device does the reverse, pressing cloth flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned iron heated on a stove and used for smoothing clothes, which flattens rather than puffs up.

clue.text: Jock's official, providing security that is

parts.note: bail is money given as security for release
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's officer guaranteeing protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword shorthand for a Scot; a bailie is a Scottish town magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a bailie is a municipal magistrate or councillor, a local civic official.

clue.text: The city fighting's cut off endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: war is fighting
sawn means cut off with a saw

explanation.surface: A town whose fighting has been brought to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as is, joining fighting to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is a specific example of a city: the Polish capital, on the Vistula river.

clue.text: Severe trial or pact?

parts.note: taken as written
a pact is a deal

explanation.surface: Choosing between a harsh test and an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or difficult experience; historically a trial by physical test.
